findings.snippet: ‖r • deriv (fun s => Implications.bochnerRiesz α s f x) r‖ₑ ^ 2 /
findings.explanation: deriv is 0 where the function is not differentiable
findings.review: Open question for a human, believed harmless. deriv returns 0 where r ↦ B_r^α f(x) is not differentiable, which would shrink the square function and weaken the statement. For Schwartz f, polar coordinates and ρ = r t give B_r^α f(x) = c r^n ∫_0^1 (1 - t²)^α t^(n-1) F_x(r t) dt with F_x smooth, which is smooth in r > 0 for every α > -1; so for α > 1/2 the junk branch never fires. The statement does not say so (no differentiability conjunct), and nothing here checks the argument. CoResearcher agent analysis (not machine-checked); a human should confirm
